howDoI.q: How do I make a boss that is bigger than one block?
How do I make a boss that guards the way to the door?
How do I make a star hit a monster that stands higher up?
How do I make a monster blink red when it is hit?
How do I make a monster that cannot be hurt for a moment?
How do I change how a monster looks after the first hit?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

The Giant is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels about a boss that is bigger than one block, and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Enter throws a star the way you last walked. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

The one idea

A monster is one block, 20 by 20 pixels, and never bigger. So a giant is several monsters standing side by side, each with its own picture, each hit on its own. Four monsters in a square make a boss two blocks wide and two high. This game also takes the idea of a boss that takes several hits from Big Bug, and the chain a monster “becomes” from Three Phases; look at those first if the word becomes is new.

pages.head: Level 1: The Giant
pages.html:
Level 1: The Giant

The THE GIANT IS 4 MONSTERS sign stands near the start. Rocky, a big grumpy fellow made of stone, fills a low tunnel through a brick wall, with the exit door on the far side. He is four monsters, two on top of two, and every part pops on one star. The STAND ON THE STEP FOR ITS HEAD sign says the rest: Rima’s star flies level with his hand, so from the ground it meets only the bottom two. Walk up on the little step and it meets the head. When all four are gone the tunnel is open. Six coins lie along the way, and one sits on the step.

Try throwing at the head from the ground once. The star flies under it and does nothing.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • One picture, cut in four. Rocky was drawn as a single 40 by 40 picture in code, then cut along the middle into four 20 by 20 pieces. Open giant.mbl in the blocks editor: gol_tl0 (top left), gol_tr0, gol_bl0 and gol_br0 are the pieces, and each has a second frame (1) so he wiggles. Placed side by side they read as one picture.
  • Four monsters. In the monsters editor, monsters 6, 7, 8 and 9 are the four parts. Each uses its own piece, has Power 150 and, when destroyed, becomes monster 5, the puff. They have no path, so they stand still.
  • Where they stand. Open one.map in the map editor. Four monsters are placed in the tunnel, 6 and 7 side by side on the top row, 8 and 9 on the bottom row. Every part is Solid on all sides, so Rima cannot walk through, and the way to the door opens only when the last one is gone.
  • Stars win, touching loses. A star has Power 200 and kills anything weaker. A touch from Rima cannot kill anything with Power 100 or more, so only stars count. Each part gives 20 points when a star pops it.
  • Which part a star finds. A star flies in a straight line, level with the spot where Rima’s Throw sequence gives it birth (the frame at 0 across and 20 down from his top, which is the row of his lower block). From the ground that is the bottom row; from a one-block step it is the top row. The step is only grass blocks on one.map.
  • No part tells the others. A monster that dies cannot say so to the rest. The way opens because the parts that blocked it are gone, nothing more.

pages.head: Level 2: Ouch, Wait
pages.html:
Level 2: Ouch, Wait

The A HIT PART BLINKS RED sign comes first. Beep, a tin robot, stands in the tunnel, and he is four monsters again, but each part takes two hits. Hit a part once and it cracks, blinks red for about two seconds and cannot be hurt; the WAIT FOR IT TO STOP sign says to hold your stars. A star thrown at a blinking part flies straight through it and hits whatever stands behind. When the blink stops the part is cracked, and the second hit pops it. Do the bottom pair from the ground and the top pair from the step. Seven coins lie along the way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Three monsters a part. Each of the four parts is a short chain. Monsters 10 to 13 are the fresh parts; 14 to 17 are the hurt parts; 18 to 21 are the cracked parts. A fresh part becomes the matching hurt part when a star kills it, a hurt part becomes the matching cracked part, and a cracked part becomes the puff, monster 5.
  • The blink. In the monsters editor, monster 14’s two pictures are crk_tl0 (the cracked part) and hot_tl (the same part tinted red), five ticks each, so it flashes about twice a second. It is one small part, never the whole screen.
  • Hurt for a moment. A hurt part has For a set time 40, about two seconds (the game clock runs 18 ticks a second). When the time is up it dies, and When destroyed it becomes turns it into the cracked part, in the same place. That is how it comes back with no one to trigger it.
  • Why a star goes through. A hurt part has Power 200, the same as a star. When two monsters of equal power meet, neither kills the other, so the star carries on and meets whatever is behind. A fresh or cracked part has Power 150, so the star wins. Touching never hurts it either way: nothing Rima does by touch kills Power 100 or more.
  • The cracks. They are only paint: crk_tl0 is the same piece as rob_tl0 with a few dark lines. Compare them in giant.mbl.
  • The score. Fresh and cracked parts give 20 points when a star pops them. The hurt part gives nothing, and neither does running out of time.
  • The map. Open two.map. Only the four fresh parts (10, 11, 12, 13) are placed.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine’s limits, so you can plan around them.

  • A monster is one block. A big boss is several monsters, and each one has its own hit points (its own chain). Nothing makes them one boss: no part knows how the others are doing, and the game cannot say “all four are gone” to open something. This level works because the four parts physically fill the tunnel.
  • Parts that move drift apart. When a part becomes the next monster, its path starts again from where it stands, so a giant that walks would shear into pieces after the first hit. These two stand still.
  • Stars fly flat. A star flies level with Rima’s hand and does not aim, so each row of a giant needs its own spot to stand on.
  • No tint. A monster cannot be tinted on the fly. The red blink is a second picture drawn red, and so is every other change of look.
  • The blink is a fixed time. A hurt part comes back after the same number of ticks every time. It does not wait for a star to leave, and nothing can make it blink for longer.
  • Equal power does nothing. A hurt part is not “immune”; it just has the same power as the star, and anything with a higher power would still kill it.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In giant.mon, set monster 6’s When destroyed it becomes to monster 7’s number, so the top left part takes two hits.
  • Change For a set time on a hurt part (monster 14) from 40 to 20 and then to 90.
  • Draw your own parts in giant.mbl: change the red pictures to purple.
  • Move the step on one.map and see where a star flies from.
  • Make a hurt part’s Power 250: a star now loses to it, and a star no longer passes.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
